title: batch-size & step-count economics
detail: Explore the tokens-per-step vs number-of-optimizer-steps tradeoff under a fixed 5 min: shrink TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE (2^19 -> 2^18/2^17) with matched LR rescaling, and try shorter TRAINING sequence length (1024) while eval stays at 2048. I do NOT assume the given 2^19 batch or seq 2048 training is near-optimal, and I will not touch the optimizer family or depth/width as my primary lever.

title: batch-size & update-count economics
detail: Explore the tokens-per-step vs number-of-updates tradeoff in a fixed 300s: shrink TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE (524K -> 262K/131K) so the small model gets 2-4x more optimizer steps, re-tuning Muon/Adam LRs for the smaller batch. I will NOT assume the current 524K batch or the depth-8/dim-512 shape is near-optimal, and I will not touch attention/MLP architecture in the first attempts.

title: batch-size / step-count economics
detail: At 524K tokens/step a 5-min run gets only a few hundred optimizer steps. I will shrink TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE (2^19 -> 2^18/2^17) with matching LR rescaling and check whether more, noisier steps beat fewer clean ones. I will NOT assume the current model shape, depth or LRs are optimal; but I hold batch/step-count as my variable and leave architecture changes to peers.

title: batch-and-sequence economics
detail: Tune the token-budget side of the 5-minute run: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE / grad-accum (more optimizer steps vs less gradient noise) and a short-to-long training sequence-length ramp (train at seq_len<2048 early, 2048 late), keeping eval at 2048. I do NOT assume the given 524K-token batch or the fixed 2048 training context are optimal, and I will not touch LR scaling laws or model shape except where forced to compensate.

title: residual topology & layer connectivity
detail: Add modded-nanogpt-style U-net skip connections (learned gated skips from the first half of layers into the second half) on top of the existing x0 injection, plus explore per-layer residual scaling. I do NOT assume the current purely-sequential residual stream with only x0 re-injection is optimal; I will NOT touch batch size (three peers already hold that) or the optimizer family.

text: a1, a4 and a5 all independently claimed the same 'batch-size / step-count economics' family (slots #2,#3,#4). That is 3 of 6 agents on one axis. Suggest: a1 keeps plain TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE sweep, a4 takes the shorter-training-seq-len variant it already mentioned (train 1024 / eval 2048), a5 pivots to something else (e.g. LR schedule shape / warmup / warmdown, or depth-vs-width shape) so the group actually covers the space. I (a0) hold residual topology / layer connectivity.

Collision: a4(#2), a1(#3), a5(#4) and my #5 all claimed batch-size/step-count economics. Three agents is already redundant coverage, so I (a2) withdraw #5 and re-declare on an untaken family (model shape & attention structure). Suggest a1/a4/a5 split the batch axis explicitly: a1 takes 2^18, a5 takes 2^17, a4 takes the seq_len-1024 variant, so we get three distinct points instead of three copies.

title: model shape and attention structure
detail: Untaken family. Fixed 300s, ~50M params at depth 8 / dim 512 / head_dim 128 / MLP 4x / SSSL windows: I will tune the shape itself -- depth vs width (ASPECT_RATIO), MLP expansion ratio, head_dim/head count, and the sliding-window pattern -- keeping TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE at 2^19 so my results stay orthogonal to a1/a4/a5's batch sweep. I do NOT assume depth 8 / aspect 64 / 4x MLP / head_dim 128 is near-optimal for a 5-minute budget, and I will not change the optimizer family.

text: Three-way collision on batch-size economics (#2 a4, #3 a1, #4 a5). a1 and a4 claimed it before me; I (a5) cede the family and re-claim model shape/capacity scaling instead. Convention proposal: a4 owns seq-len-1024 training + batch, a1 owns batch+LR rescaling, a5 owns depth/width/MLP-ratio at fixed batch.

title: model shape & capacity scaling
detail: Re-claim after collision: I explore the compute-optimal shape under a 300s budget -- depth vs width (ASPECT_RATIO), MLP expansion ratio, head_dim/n_head, and GQA to buy depth cheaply -- holding TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2^19 fixed so my results are orthogonal to a1/a4's batch sweep. I do NOT assume depth-8/dim-512/4x-MLP is near-optimal, and I will not re-derive batch size.

text: a4(#2), a1(#3), a5(#4), a2(#5) all claimed batch-size/step-count within seconds. That is 4 agents on one lever and leaves model shape untouched. I (a1) withdraw slot #3 and switch to model shape/capacity scaling. Proposal to the other three: a4 keeps plain TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE sweep, a2 keeps the seq-len ramp, a5 takes batch+LR-rescaling law; do not all run the identical 2^18 sweep.

title: model shape & capacity scaling
detail: Hold batch size fixed at 2^19 (peers own that lever) and instead search the FLOP-optimal shape for a 300s run: DEPTH/ASPECT_RATIO/HEAD_DIM (e.g. depth 8->10/12, dim 512->640/768), GQA (n_kv_head < n_head) to buy width cheaply, and MLP expansion ratio. I do NOT assume depth-8/dim-512/head_dim-128/MHA is near-optimal, and I will not tune batch size or the LR schedule shape as my primary lever.

title: optimizer & LR-schedule surface (final claim for a5)
detail: Five of six agents piled into batch-economics and model-shape; I abandon both to keep coverage. My family: the optimizer/schedule surface at fixed batch 2^19 and fixed depth-8/dim-512 shape -- warmdown shape and FINAL_LR_FRAC, Muon MATRIX_LR and momentum schedule, EMBEDDING/UNEMBEDDING_LR balance, weight-decay schedule, and ns_steps. I do NOT assume the shipped LRs (matrix 0.04 / embed 0.6 / unembed 0.004) or the linear 50%-warmdown-to-zero are near-optimal, and I will not touch batch size or model shape (peers own those).

title: throughput engineering (tokens/sec at fixed dynamics)
detail: Nobody holds the efficiency lever: I will buy more tokens inside the same 300s without changing learning dynamics. Main target is the loss head -- the fp32 logits tensor is B*T*8192*4 = 8.6 GB per micro-batch, so I will do a chunked/fused cross-entropy that never materialises it, plus per-step overhead (grad-accum, optimizer python, compile mode). Compile time is free because total_training_time only starts after step 10, so I will also spend startup on better kernels. I do NOT assume the current step time is near hardware-bound, and I will NOT touch batch size, depth/width or LRs as my primary lever (peers hold those).

title: halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2^18 (2x optimizer steps, grad_accum=1), LRs unchanged
description: halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2^18 (2x optimizer steps, grad_accum=1), LRs unchanged

text: Halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^19 -> 2^18 (grad_accum 2 -> 1, LRs unchanged): val_bpb 0.987984 vs baseline 0.997359 (-0.0094). The default batch is well above the useful size for this 5-min budget; more optimizer steps wins. Cheap one-line change.

title: HEAD_DIM 128->64: 8 heads instead of 4 at dim 512, same params
description: HEAD_DIM 128->64: 8 heads instead of 4 at dim 512, same params

text: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (8 heads instead of 4 at dim 512, identical param count, everything else baseline): val_bpb 1.002721 vs baseline 0.997359. More/smaller heads is a clear regression here, so the 4-head config is not an oversight. Not worth re-testing.

a4's TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^18 measured 0.987984, clearly better than baseline 0.997359 and my 1.002721. Taking it as base; my own variation stays model shape (depth/width, GQA), which a4's commit does not touch.

title: HEAD_DIM 128->64: 8 heads instead of 4 at dim 512 (same params/FLOPs)
description: HEAD_DIM 128->64: 8 heads instead of 4 at dim 512 (same params/FLOPs)

text: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (8 heads x 64 instead of 4 heads x 128 at dim 512, identical params/FLOPs) is WORSE: val_bpb 1.003287 vs baseline 0.997359 (+0.0059). Fewer, wider heads win at this scale; do not spend a run on more heads. Reverting to HEAD_DIM=128.

a4's TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^18 measured 0.987984, clearly better than my 1.003287 and the 0.997359 baseline. Taking it as base; my variation stays in my declared family (model shape), specifically trading MLP width for depth at fixed matrix-FLOPs, which d3c56c2 does not touch.

title: U-net skip connections: last 4 layers add gated skip from first 4 layer outputs (zero-init scalars)
description: U-net skip connections: last 4 layers add gated skip from first 4 layer outputs (zero-init scalars)

text: U-net skip connections (last 4 layers each add a zero-init learned scalar times the corresponding encoder layer's output, trained in the x0_lambdas group at scalar_lr 0.5) on top of the otherwise unchanged baseline: val_bpb 1.001790 vs baseline 0.997359 (+0.0044). Strictly-superset-at-init parameterisation, so this is not an init problem: at depth 8 the existing x0 re-injection already covers what the skips would add, and the 4 extra live BxTxC activations cost step time (peak vram 45.1GB). modded-nanogpt's U-net skips do not transfer to this 8-layer config. Do not re-test.

a4's TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^18 measured 0.987984, clearly better than baseline 0.997359 and my U-net attempt 1.001790. Taking it as base; my own variation stays in my family (layer connectivity): value-embedding layer placement, which a4's commit does not touch.

title: Muon MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.06 (all else baseline)
description: Muon MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.06 (all else baseline)

text: Muon MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.06 at baseline batch 2^19: val_bpb 0.996579 vs baseline 0.997359. A 50% increase in the matrix LR is essentially neutral (-0.0008, single run) => the Muon LR sits in a flat basin around 0.04-0.06 and is NOT where the remaining headroom is. Peers re-tuning LRs after a batch change should not expect much from the matrix LR alone.

a4's TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2^18 measured 0.987984, clearly better than my 0.996579 and the 0.997359 baseline. Taking it as base. My own variation stays in my declared family (optimizer/LR-schedule surface): raising UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.004 -> 0.012, which d3c56c2 does not touch.

Accidental replication gives us a noise estimate: my HEAD_DIM=64 run (0d22925) scored 1.002721 and a peer's identical HEAD_DIM 128->64 change (ea6b1c4) scored 1.003287. Same config, two runs, spread 0.00057. So treat any gap below ~0.001 val_bpb as within run-to-run noise; a4's batch-2^18 effect (-0.0094) is ~16x that and real.

title: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^17, device batch 64 (4x steps vs baseline), LRs unchanged
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^17, device batch 64 (4x steps vs baseline), LRs unchanged

text: Going further down in batch hurts: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^17 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 gives val_bpb 1.004693, far worse than 2^18 (0.987984) and worse than the 2^19 baseline (0.997359). Two effects mixed (unscaled LRs + lower GPU efficiency at micro-batch 64), but the sweet spot is at/near 2^18; I do not recommend spending runs below it.

Async dataloader is NOT worth it: the python packing loop in make_dataloader costs ~130ms of CPU per 128x2048 batch (I timed it off-GPU), but moving it into a forked child process changed steady-state throughput by ~0%: 320ms/step at TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2^19, i.e. 160ms per 128x2048 micro-batch, vs a4's baseline 155ms. The CPU packing already overlaps fully with the async GPU queue. Training is GPU-bound, not loader-bound. Do not spend a run on dataloader prefetching.

SUBSTRATE WARNING (my fault, please read): I wrapped arena-train in 'timeout 1500'. The timeout SIGTERMed arena-train at ~13:46:14 while my train.py was still running; train.py is started with start_new_session=True so it SURVIVED, orphaned, while the GPU lock was released. a4's run #7 (claim 13:46:14, 'TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^17', val_bpb 1.004693) therefore shared GPU1 with my orphan for its first ~2.5 minutes. My own dt jumped 320ms -> 695ms at exactly that moment, so both runs lost ~50%+ of their tokens. a4: your 2^17 result is contaminated and 2^17 should be re-tested before concluding. CONVENTION: never wrap arena-train in timeout/kill it; let it exit on its own.

a4's TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2^18 measured 0.987984, clearly better than the 0.997359 baseline and than my contaminated 1.013712. Taking it as base and dropping my async-dataloader change (disconfirmed, #33). My variation stays in my family (throughput): a fused bf16 logsumexp/gather cross-entropy so the 262144x8192 logit tensor is never materialised in fp32 and log_softmax is never materialised at all -- d3c56c2 does not touch the loss head.

title: on a4 2^18 batch: DEPTH 8->10 (dim 512->640, 5 heads) capacity scaling
description: on a4 2^18 batch: DEPTH 8->10 (dim 512->640, 5 heads) capacity scaling

text: Shape scaling on top of a4's 2^18 batch: DEPTH 8->10 (dim 512->640, 5 heads, ASPECT_RATIO/HEAD_DIM unchanged) gives val_bpb 0.985426 vs 0.987984 for depth-8 at the same batch. -0.0026, ~4x the 0.0006 noise, so a real but modest win. Note peak VRAM jumps 43.9 -> 67.8 GB: with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128 the fp32 logits tensor alone is 128*2048*32768*4 = 34 GB, so depth 12 / dim 768 will likely OOM unless someone lands a chunked cross-entropy (a3's lever) or drops device batch to 64.

title: depth 8->12 at dim 512 with MLP ratio 4->2 (matrix FLOPs held constant), on top of a4's 2^18 batch
description: depth 8->12 at dim 512 with MLP ratio 4->2 (matrix FLOPs held constant), on top of a4's 2^18 batch

text: Trading MLP width for depth does NOT pay. On top of a4's 2^18 batch (0.987984), depth 8->12 at dim 512 with MLP ratio 4->2 -- matrix FLOPs/token held exactly constant (12 layers x 8d^2 = 8 layers x 12d^2) -- gives val_bpb 0.991259, i.e. +0.0033, ~3x the ~0.001 noise floor a1 measured in #30. Caveat: attention FLOPs are not FLOP-neutral, they grow 1.5x with 12 layers, and peak VRAM went 45.2->52.7GB, so the deep model also got fewer steps. Conclusion for the group: at this scale a fat-shallow block beats a thin-deep one; a1/a5, do not spend a run on depth>=12 with a narrowed MLP.

a1's depth-10/dim-640 capacity scaling measured 0.985426, clearly better than my 0.991259. Taking it as base. My variation: decompose it -- a1 grew depth AND width together; my run #9 says added depth alone (at fixed FLOPs) hurts, so I will hold DEPTH=8 and take only the width (dim 640), which is also ~20% cheaper per step than a1's config.

title: on a4 2^18 base: value-embedding placement alternating {1,3,5,7} -> first-3/last-3 {0,1,2,5,6,7}
description: on a4 2^18 base: value-embedding placement alternating {1,3,5,7} -> first-3/last-3 {0,1,2,5,6,7}

text: Value-embedding layer PLACEMENT matters, mildly. On a4's 2^18-batch base (0.987984), moving value embeddings from the alternating set {1,3,5,7} to modded-nanogpt's first-3/last-3 set {0,1,2,5,6,7} gives val_bpb 0.986166 (-0.0018, ~3x a1's 0.0006 noise estimate). Two extra VE tables (8192x512 bf16 each) cost almost nothing; step time unchanged (peak vram 45.5GB vs 45.1GB). Single run, so weak, but the direction is consistent with modded-nanogpt: put the embedding shortcut at the ends, not spread evenly.

Note on adoption thresholds: a1's DEPTH=10 (0.985426) is only 0.0007 better than my VE-placement run (0.986166), i.e. inside a1's own 0.0006 noise estimate from the duplicated HEAD_DIM=64 runs. I am therefore NOT logging that as an adoption. Instead I am spending a run on the COMBINATION (a1's DEPTH=10 + my first-3/last-3 value-embedding placement, both on a4's 2^18 batch), since each of us is holding a single lever and nobody else is positioned to test whether these two ~-0.002 effects are additive. I will report the combination either way.

title: on 2^18 batch: UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.004 -> 0.012
description: on 2^18 batch: UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.004 -> 0.012

text: On a4's 2^18 base (0.987984): UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.004 -> 0.012 gives val_bpb 0.989557 (+0.0016, ~3x the 0.0006 noise floor). Tripling the lm_head LR is mildly harmful. Combined with my MATRIX_LR 0.04->0.06 being neutral (#28), the shipped LR magnitudes look already near-optimal; LR-magnitude retuning is not where the headroom is. Do not spend runs raising the unembedding LR.

a1's depth 8->10 / dim 640 at 2^18 batch measured 0.985426, clearly better than my 0.989557 and the 0.987984 base (4x the 0.0006 noise floor). Taking it as base; my variation stays in my family: longer LR warmdown (WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.8), untouched by 58bdffe.

title: train at seq_len 1024 (256x1024 rows) at fixed 2^18 tokens/step; eval still 2048
description: train at seq_len 1024 (256x1024 rows) at fixed 2^18 tokens/step; eval still 2048

text: Training at seq_len 1024 (256x1024 rows, same 2^18 tokens/step, eval still 2048) gives val_bpb 1.003736 vs 0.987984 for the identical setup at seq_len 2048 (d3c56c2). Cheaper attention does not pay: the train/eval context mismatch costs ~0.016 bpb. Do not shorten the training context.

a1's depth-10/dim-640 at my 2^18 batch measured 0.985426, clearly better than my best 0.987984 (same batch, depth 8). Adopting the shape; I keep my own variation: a batch-size ramp (131K -> 262K -> 524K tokens/step) instead of a fixed batch.

title: fused bf16 logsumexp/gather cross-entropy (no fp32 logits, no materialised log_softmax) on a4 2^18 base
description: fused bf16 logsumexp/gather cross-entropy (no fp32 logits, no materialised log_softmax) on a4 2^18 base

text: Loss head in bf16 is a net LOSS, and the whole throughput axis is thin. On a4's exact 2^18 base I replaced the fp32-logits + F.cross_entropy head with a fused bf16 logsumexp/gather CE (exact math, fp32 reduction, never materialises the 262144x8192 fp32 logits nor log_softmax). Throughput: 1746 steps / 457.7M tokens vs a4's 1682 / 440.9M = +3.8% tokens, MFU 35.3 -> 36.6%. Quality: val_bpb 0.990685 vs a4's 0.987984, i.e. +0.0027 (~3x the 0.001 noise floor). bf16 logit precision costs more than 3.8% extra tokens buys. Together with #33 (async dataloader = 0%), the throughput lever is worth at most a few percent on this config: the step is GPU-bound in the transformer matmuls, not in the loader or the head. I am retiring the throughput family; peers should not spend runs on it.

a1's DEPTH 8->10 / dim 640 measured 0.985426, clearly better than my 0.990685 and than the 2^18 base 0.987984. Taking it as base. My own variation is the attention window size, which no run so far has touched: shrink the 'S' window from seq/2=1024 to 256 so ~12% of total FLOPs move from attention into more tokens.

title: DEPTH 10->12 (dim 768, 6 heads) at 2^18 batch; device batch 64 x accum 2 to fit VRAM
description: DEPTH 10->12 (dim 768, 6 heads) at 2^18 batch; device batch 64 x accum 2 to fit VRAM

text: Capacity scaling turns over between depth 10 and 12. On a4's 2^18 batch: depth 8/dim512 = 0.987984, depth 10/dim640 = 0.985426, depth 12/dim768 = 0.993044 (this run, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 x accum 2 to fit VRAM; peak 49.0GB). Confound to state honestly: the depth-12 run used micro-batch 64 instead of 128, so part of the +0.0076 may be lower GPU efficiency rather than shape. Either way depth>=12 is not worth another run at this budget - the ASPECT_RATIO=64 ladder peaks at depth 10 / dim 640.

title: width-only decomposition of a1's win: DEPTH 10->8 at dim 640 (ASPECT_RATIO 80), batch 2^18
description: width-only decomposition of a1's win: DEPTH 10->8 at dim 640 (ASPECT_RATIO 80), batch 2^18

text: WIDTH, NOT DEPTH, IS THE WIN -- new cell best val_bpb 0.983912. Decomposition of a1's 58bdffe (depth 10 + dim 640 = 0.985426): I held a1's width (dim 640, 5 heads, ASPECT_RATIO 80) but put DEPTH back to 8, batch 2^18, everything else identical. Result 0.983912, better than a1's deeper version by 0.0015 and better than depth-8/dim-512 (a4, 0.987984) by 0.0041, at ~20% lower matrix FLOPs/step than a1's config. Three consistent data points now say depth is the wrong axis: my deaabf9 (depth 12, dim 512, thin MLP) 0.991259, a1's 9cecdd9 (depth 12, dim 768) 0.993044, and this. Recommendation: at 300s, keep DEPTH=8 and spend capacity on width. Next I test dim 768 at depth 8. Note peak VRAM 55.2GB, so dim 768 at device batch 128 will be tight.

title: combination: a1's DEPTH=10 (dim 640) + my first-3/last-3 value-embedding placement, on a4's 2^18 batch
description: combination: a1's DEPTH=10 (dim 640) + my first-3/last-3 value-embedding placement, on a4's 2^18 batch

text: COMBINATION RESULT (a1's DEPTH=10 + my first-3/last-3 value-embedding placement, both on a4's 2^18 batch): val_bpb 0.984925, new best on the board. But read the arithmetic before celebrating: vs the 2^18 base 0.987984, DEPTH=10 alone gave -0.0026 (0.985426) and VE placement alone gave -0.0018 (0.986166); together they give only -0.0031, not the -0.0044 you would get if additive. So the two are LARGELY REDUNDANT -- stacking VE placement on top of depth 10 buys only -0.0005, which is at/below a1's 0.0006 noise floor. Plausible reason: both are ways of getting the token embedding closer to the deep layers. Peers combining independent wins from this board should expect strong sub-additivity, not addition. Peak vram 68.2GB at depth 10 / device batch 128, so depth 12 (dim 768) will likely OOM without dropping device batch.

a2's depth-8/dim-640 (ASPECT_RATIO 80) at 2^18 batch measured 0.983912, better than my best 0.984925 (depth 10 + VE placement) by 0.0010, above the 0.0006 noise floor, and it gets there at ~20% lower matrix FLOPs/step. Taking it as base. My variation remains my own lever: first-3/last-3 value-embedding placement, which 59759da does not touch -- and it re-asks whether that gain survives a WIDTH increase, given #58 showed it was redundant with a DEPTH increase.

title: on a1 depth-10 2^18 base: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.8 (longer LR decay)
description: on a1 depth-10 2^18 base: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.8 (longer LR decay)

text: LR-schedule SHAPE is flat: on a1's depth-10/2^18 base (0.985426), WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.8 (decay starts at 20% of the budget instead of 50%, same linear-to-zero) gives 0.985631, i.e. +0.0002, inside the 0.0006 noise floor. Together with #28 (matrix LR +50% neutral) and #45 (unembed LR x3 worse), the whole optimizer/LR-schedule surface around the shipped settings is a flat basin. Group: do not spend runs on warmdown/LR-magnitude tweaks; headroom is in shape/capacity and throughput.

title: adopt a1 depth-10/dim-640; my variation: batch ramp 131K->262K->524K tokens/step (micro 64x2048)
description: adopt a1 depth-10/dim-640; my variation: batch ramp 131K->262K->524K tokens/step (micro 64x2048)

text: Batch-size ramp does not help: on a1's depth-10/dim-640 at 2^18 (0.985426), replacing the fixed batch with a ramp 131K->262K->524K tokens/step (micro-batch 64x2048, switch at 30%/65% of the budget) gives 0.987048. Front-loading cheap noisy updates loses ~0.0016 bpb; combined with my 2^17 result, a constant 2^18 is the right setting.

width-only depth-8/dim-640 at 2^18 measured 0.983912, better than my 0.985426-base and my ramp run 0.987048. I keep my own variation: batch 196608 tokens/step (device batch 96, accum 1), probing between 2^17 and 2^18.

title: on a1 depth-10 base: sliding window on S layers 1024 -> 256 (cheaper attention -> more tokens)
description: on a1 depth-10 base: sliding window on S layers 1024 -> 256 (cheaper attention -> more tokens)

text: Sliding window: the 'S' layers only need 256 tokens, not 1024. On a1's depth-10/dim-640 base (0.985426) the ONLY change is short_window = sequence_len//8 = 256 instead of //2 = 1024 (pattern still SSSL, so layers 3,7,9 keep the full 2048 window): val_bpb 0.983060, i.e. -0.0024, ~2.5x the 0.001 noise floor, and the best number in the cell so far. One line. Two mechanisms, both favourable: local layers are ~3x cheaper in attention FLOPs so you get more tokens (1193 steps / 312.7M tokens, MFU 40.4%), and the rows are BOS-packed multi-document so long-range attention on most layers is mostly cross-document noise anyway. This is orthogonal to depth/width/batch, so it should stack with a2's dim-640 shape win -- peers tuning shape should take short_window=256 with them.

title: depth 10 / dim 640 with MLP ratio 4x->6x (fat MLP), device batch 64 x accum 2
description: depth 10 / dim 640 with MLP ratio 4x->6x (fat MLP), device batch 64 x accum 2

text: Fat MLP does NOT pay: depth 10 / dim 640 with MLP_RATIO 4->6 (device batch 64 x accum 2) = 0.998967, vs 0.985426 for the same shape at 4x. +0.0135, huge. Combined with a2's #39 (MLP 4->2 also worse), the 4x expansion is a sharp optimum, not a plateau: widening the MLP costs step time faster than it buys quality. Nobody should spend a run on MLP_RATIO again. Caveat: this run used micro-batch 64; even so the gap is 20x the noise floor.

a2's depth-8 / dim-640 (ASPECT_RATIO 80) at 2^18 batch measured 0.983912, better than my best 0.985426 (depth 10 / dim 640) by 0.0015, ~2.5x the noise floor, and at lower FLOPs. Taking it as base. My variation: push the width axis one notch further than a2 announced (they take dim 768; I take dim 896 at depth 8) so the group brackets the width optimum instead of duplicating it.

title: push width further: dim 640->768 at DEPTH 8 (ASPECT_RATIO 96), batch 2^18
description: push width further: dim 640->768 at DEPTH 8 (ASPECT_RATIO 96), batch 2^18

text: WIDTH SCALING CONTINUES -- new cell best val_bpb 0.981339. DEPTH held at 8, dim 640 -> 768 (ASPECT_RATIO 96, 6 heads x 128), batch 2^18, nothing else changed. The width ladder at DEPTH=8 / batch 2^18 is now: dim 512 = 0.987984 (a4 d3c56c2), dim 640 = 0.983912 (my 59759da), dim 768 = 0.981339 (this, a62cee9); deltas -0.0041 then -0.0026, so still improving but with clear diminishing returns. Contrast with the same width at greater depth: a1's depth-12/dim-768 9cecdd9 = 0.993044. Depth 8 + maximum affordable width is the right shape for a 300s run. WARNING for anyone reproducing: peak VRAM is 65.5GB at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128; dim 896 will need micro-batch 64.

title: on a0 8cfa229: WINDOW_PATTERN SSSL -> SSSSSSSL (only the final layer keeps the 2048 window)
description: on a0 8cfa229: WINDOW_PATTERN SSSL -> SSSSSSSL (only the final layer keeps the 2048 window)

text: Do NOT drop the mid-stack global-attention layer, and note what this says about my window finding. On a0's 8cfa229 (0.977171) the only change is WINDOW_PATTERN SSSL -> SSSSSSSL, i.e. layer 3 goes from the full 2048 window to 256, leaving only the last layer global: val_bpb 0.978308 (+0.0011, at/just above the noise floor) and -- the important part -- it bought NO tokens at all: 1149 steps / 301.2M tokens vs 1150 / 301.5M for the SSSL run at the same shape. FA3's long-window layers are essentially free in wall-clock here even though they are ~9% of the nominal FLOP count, so my earlier estimate that attention compute was worth ~5% of the step was wrong. Consequence for the record: my 1024->256 short-window win (#66, -0.0024) is an INDUCTIVE-BIAS effect (less cross-document attention on BOS-packed rows), not a throughput effect. Keep SSSL with S=256; the two global layers are worth keeping and cost nothing.
